 'Last of my issues': Kwesi Appiah not afraid of sack as Sudan face Senegal
 Dennis Mabuka Sudan national team coach Kwesi Appiah Sudan National Team Sudan national team coach Kwesi Appiah has maintained he is not afraid of losing his role as the team prepares to face Senegal in their matchday four fixture of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers at Juba National Stadium on Tuesday.
 The Falcons of Jediane are struggling in the qualifiers having won one game from three matches, and are currently sitting third in Group J.
 Sudan won their first qualifying game 1-0 against Ethiopia, but lost the second 4-1 against Mozambique, before the 4-1 thrashing against Senegal in their matchday three, which served as a double-header.
 Sudan’s performance has elicited debate across the East African nation with a section of fans demanding for the sacking of Appiah , who was officially appointed in September 2023 on a three-year contract, and his deal was later extended until 2029.
 The Ghanaian coach guided Sudan through a strong FIFA World Cup qualifying campaign and qualified the team for AFCON 2025 in Morocco.

 VIEW MATCH DETAILS Appiah has explained he does not fear dismissal, and that his focus is on performing his duties and giving his utmost effort, pointing out the challenges the team is facing due to the suspension of the local league and the participation of players from other leagues.
 "If you are afraid to be sacked, then why are you doing the job? You should get out of the job right from day one,"  said Appiah.
 "I’m not the kind of coach, who’s afraid even one day to be told to go out, but I believe that as a coach you go out there, do your best to make sure you get the results that you can.
 "If you cannot get the result and the players play tactically and everything is going well according to your plan, then automatically, you’ve done your part. 
 "At the end of the day, it’s up to the management or whoever to decide whether you stay or go, but on my part, it’s is the last of my issues."
 On whether Sudan still stands a chance to qualify, and play at the 2027 AFCON in East Africa, Appiah said: " You know sometimes in this competition sometimes you can never say it’s finished until the end of the competition. 
 "Because anything can beat you along the line. I believe that Sudan can qualify irrespective of whether they have won or lost.
 "We still have some games to play, and the most important thing is to make sure between your mind, and inside your players is to make sure they perform at the highest level each and every day." 
 Appiah continued: "We all know there is no league in Sudan, Al Hilal Club (Omdurman), and Al Merrikh SC are playing in Rwanda, but players in Europe and even Australia are playing actively."
 Appiah acknowledged the presence of mistakes and tactical discipline that was not required in the previous match, confirming that they are working on fixing them.
 "I believe that going forward we have learnt our mistakes, and we will make sure we do the right thing tomorrow (Tuesday) against Senegal," explained Appiah.
 "We will fight until the end, and I know it’s going to be a very good game, and I hope the fans will enjoy it. It’s not going to be an easy game because we all know Senegal’s caliber, but we are ready." 
 Zambia ready for Burundi 
 Meanwhile, Zambia defender Ricky Chanda says the team is ready for Tuesday’s qualifier against Burundi.
 In an interview with the FAZ Media, Chanda said he was happy that the technical bench was giving many youngsters an opportunity to play for the Chipolopolo.
 "Everything right now is going well; we had recovery training today. Right now, we are getting back to shape. We are ready for Tuesday’s match,” said the 21-year-old, who is on the books of Estonian side FC Nomme United.
 On playing away in Bujumbura, he said: " We had home fans and it will obviously be difficult since all the home fans will be cheering the home team." 
 The Chipolopolo are in Bujumbura for Tuesday’s Group I POMOJA 2027 AFCON qualifier against Burundi which will be played at the Stade Intwari at 15h00 CAT. 
 Algeria tops Group I with seven points while Zambia lies second with four. Togo is third on three points while Burundi is at the bottom with two points.
